# `dotfiles`

Apply the base dotfiles and every private layer with chezmoi


- **Usage:** `dotfiles [FLAGS] [SUBCOMMAND]`

## Global Flags
- **`-n --dry-run`** — Preview without changing anything
- **`-v --verbose`** — Print each chezmoi and git command
- **`-l --layer <layer>`** — Act on one layer only

  **Choices:** output of `dotfiles layers --names`

## Flags
- **`-i --interactive`** — Open a menu of every command

## `dotfiles apply`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles apply`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Write the base, then each layer, into the home folder; stops first if two layers own one file

## `dotfiles diff`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles diff`

Show the exact changes apply would make, layer by layer

## `dotfiles doctor`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles doctor [--offline]`

Check every layer, the machine's answers, forbidden words and Homebrew drift; reports only, changes nothing

### Flags
- **`--offline`** — Skip the checks that talk to GitHub

## `dotfiles edit`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles edit [layer]`

Open a layer's repo (the base by default) in your editor

### Arguments
- **`[layer]`** — Layer name

  **Choices:** output of `dotfiles layers --names`

## `dotfiles help`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles help [command]`

List commands, or show one command's usage

### Arguments
- **`[command]`** — Command to describe

## `dotfiles hosts`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles hosts [--json]`

List tailnet machines with your descriptions and whether each is online

### Flags
- **`--json`** — Print JSON instead of a table

## `dotfiles install`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles install [FLAGS] <package>…`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Install Homebrew packages and record them in a layer's Brewfile, then commit and push

### Arguments
- **`<package>…`** — Homebrew formula or cask names

### Flags
- **`--personal`** — Record in the base's Brewfile.personal (personal machines only)
- **`--cask`** — Treat every package as a cask (casks are otherwise detected)
- **`--no-push`** — Commit but do not push

## `dotfiles layers`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles layers [--names]`

List the layers in apply order with their repo, branch and local changes

### Flags
- **`--names`** — Print only the layer names, one per line

## `dotfiles path`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles path [layer]`

Print a layer's repo folder (the base by default), as in: cd "$(dotfiles path)"

### Arguments
- **`[layer]`** — Layer name

  **Choices:** output of `dotfiles layers --names`

## `dotfiles remove`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles remove [--keep-installed] [--no-push] <package>…`
- **Aliases:** `uninstall`
- **Effect:** destructive — may delete or irreversibly overwrite

Remove packages from whichever Brewfiles list them, uninstall them, then commit and push

### Arguments
- **`<package>…`** — Homebrew formula or cask names

### Flags
- **`--keep-installed`** — Only edit the Brewfile; leave the package installed
- **`--no-push`** — Commit but do not push

## `dotfiles setup`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles setup [FLAGS]`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Set up this machine one step at a time, asking only for what is missing; safe to rerun

### Flags
- **`-y --yes`** — Take the default for every question instead of asking
- **`--redo <step>`** — Run this step's fix even if its check passes
- **`--redo-all`** — Run every step's fix
- **`--skip <step>`** — Skip this step
- **`--work <work>`** — Whether this is a work machine

  **Choices:** `yes`, `no`
- **`--git-name <name>`** — Git author name
- **`--git-email <email>`** — Git author email (the employer's address on a work machine)
- **`--personal-email <email>`** — Personal git email for personal repos
- **`--personal-host <host>`** — Personal machine's short hostname, for ssh personal
- **`--tailnet-domain <domain>`** — Domain that reaches tailnet machines by name
- **`--keychain-ref <ref>`** — 1Password op:// reference to the personal machine's login password
- **`--job-repo <repo>`** — Shared work layer repo, as owner/name

## `dotfiles status`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles status`

Show what apply would change, layer by layer (the default command)

## `dotfiles sync`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles sync`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Pull each layer's repo (fast-forward only), then apply them all

## `dotfiles version`

- **Usage:** `dotfiles version`

Print the base repo's version, from its latest tag
